name: Fastenal Company

corporate_actions.event: Q3 2026 results: sales $2.46bn (+15.5% daily), op. margin 21.5%

geography.fx_notes: ESTIMATE: US ~84%, Canada/Mexico ~13%, other ~3% based on 10-K geographic note pattern (not re-fetched). Mexico is the main EM exposure. China sourcing but negligible sales.

company_fcf.definition: Operating cash flow less net capex (company 'free cash flow'); 87% of net income

lease.source_id: US GAAP filer: operating lease cost within opex; finance leases immaterial (not disclosed in sources reviewed)

acquisitions.notes: Fastenal grows organically (branches, Onsites, FMI); no material acquisitions in period (INFERENCE from 10-K history). Reported growth approximates organic but company does not label it 'organic'.

management.senior_turnover_5y: Internal successions: Dan Florness (CEO 2016-2025) handed over to Jeff Watts; CFO also changed; promote-from-within culture
management.guidance_record: No formal revenue/EPS guidance; publishes monthly sales; capex guide $310-330m for 2026 reaffirmed

ownership.controlling_holders: None; widely held (founder Kierlin family no longer controlling)
ownership.remuneration_notes: Historically modest executive pay with incentive tied to pre-tax earnings growth (not re-verified)

A.rationale: Highly repeat MRO/production consumables with embedded supply relationships, though volumes are tied to industrial activity.

evidence: 143k installed FMI devices create switching costs [S1]
Share gains well above market growth [S1]
B.rationale: Local density plus embedded vending/Onsite create demonstrable switching costs and superior returns.

evidence: Operating margin ~21% vs most MRO peers 10-17%
C.rationale: Scale and network density measurably produce superior margins and returns.

evidence: Large fragmented MRO TAM; non-fastener and international expansion [S1]
Capex funded internally at ~3-4% of sales [S1]
D.rationale: Long organic runway with high incremental returns.

G.rationale: Conservative, high-return reinvestment; buybacks opportunistic but small.

evidence: Amazon Business/e-commerce competition for tail spend
Data centres cited as strongest growth area [S1]
I2.rationale: INFERENCE: data-centre-related demand probably 2-5% of sales; rising.

I3.rationale: Large labour-heavy SG&A base already showing productivity gains.

I4.rationale: Strong position allows retention of most savings.

K.rationale: Clean GAAP accounts with cash close to profit.

ai.notes: Data centres named as strongest growth market (Q3 2026) but not quantified; INFERENCE 2-5% of sales. Semis immaterial.

sector_specific.notes: acquisition_growth_pct 0: no material acquisitions (INFERENCE). construction: non-residential construction is a disclosed end market, historically roughly high-single-digit % of sales (not re-verified). Inventory-heavy model (PitchBook GM ~44.6%), FMI/Onsite small-ticket MRO.

gates.notes: Net cash/low leverage; FCF ~87% of NI in Q3, typically ~85-100%; no customer >15%; AI/DC <15%; US domicile; no UK consumer exposure.

bull_points: Share gains with key accounts: Q3 2026 daily sales +15.5% vs PMI ~55 market (S1)
Embedded FMI/Onsite model gives switching costs and ROIC 32.5% (S1)
SG&A leverage from technology/automation with flat headcount (S1)
bear_points: Large-account mix structurally lowers gross margin (-50bp mix headwind) (S1)
Cyclical US industrial exposure; heavy manufacturing ~45% of sales (S1)
Premium valuation historically leaves little room for a cyclical downturn (INFERENCE)
thesis_breakers: Operating margin below 19% for a full year outside a recession
Contract-customer daily sales growth below total market for 4 consecutive quarters
FMI installed base growth turning negative

sources.title: PitchBook financials Fastenal (41265-82): TTM Q4 revenue series
